title: Why Nvidia, Delta, and TSMC All Need Chroma: An Exclusive Interview with CEO I-Shih Tseng

We’re like a temple, with many monks chanting different scriptures.”

That’s how Chroma CEO I-Shih Tseng describes a company that spent decades developing technologies—sometimes long before the market knew it would need them.

Now AI has changed everything.

Nvidia relies on Chroma for system-level GPU testing. Delta Electronics is a major customer of its power-testing business. TSMC has adopted its metrology technology for advanced packaging.

And as AI chips become more expensive and complex, Tseng says testing has undergone a fundamental shift: from an economic tool used to manage yield into an absolute necessity that can determine whether a new product launches at all.

Customers have even warned Chroma that only a handful of suppliers now stand between them and their next product launch: “You’re one of them.”

So how did a Taiwanese company that spent years struggling to break into semiconductor testing become a critical link across AI chips, 800V data-center power, advanced packaging, and CPO?
